newsitem.title: USA: NFL-FAVRE GETS RICHEST NFL CONTRACT.
newsitem.headline: NFL-FAVRE GETS RICHEST NFL CONTRACT.

text.p: Brett Favre, who guided the Green Bay Packers to their first Super Bowl triumph in nearly three decades, was given a contract extension on Friday reportedly making him the highest-paid player in the National Football League.
The seven-year deal was announced Friday at a news conference at Lambeau Field, a day before the Packers host the Miami Dolphins in their preseason opener.
Terms were not disclosed, but the Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel reported that Favre has signed for seven more season.

The contract, the paper reported, includes a signing bonus of $12 million, will average between $6 million and $6.5 million per year and obligate Favre to the Packers through the 2003 season, when he will be 34.
"I'm happy we got it done, but I'm more excited about the season", said Favre, whose previous contract was through the 1998 season.

Favre's deal reportedly surpasses the five-year contract, plus an option, that the Detroit Lions gave to running back Barry Sanders earlier this week. Sanders reportedly agreed to a five-year extension with an option for a sixth worth more than $34 million. Sanders will get a signing bonus of $11.5 million.
Favre set an NFC record with 38 touchdown passes in 1995 and then eclipsed it with 39 this year.
In six NFL seasons, Favre has completed 61.9 percent of his passes for 18,724 yards and 147 touchdowns with 79 interceptions. He completed a 45-day rehabilitation stay

at the Menninger Clinic in Topeka, Kansas last year for an addiction to painkillers. He returned to Green Bay in July and announced before the start of training camp that he would take the Packers to the Super Bowl.
The Mississippi native delivered as Green Bay defeated New England for its first Super Bowl title in 29 years.
The Journal-Sentinel said the contract includes clauses to protect the Packers if Favre were to violate the league's substance-abuse policy and not be able to play.
Favre played collegiately at Southern Mississippi and was drafted by the Atlanta Falcons in 1991 before being acquired by Green Bay prior to the 1992 season.
